title: Power Apps: modern, refreshed look reaches the mail app on the semi-annual channel
summary: Hold: the licensing position is not wholly unpublished, because Microsoft documents the premium use rights required for model-driven apps. The New Look control's UI path also stops at adding a setting rather than reaching its editable value.

claims.claim: This Power Apps change extends the Fluent-based modern look for model-driven apps to the mail app.

claims.claim: Learn says the mail app look is on by default for monthly-channel environments from February 2026.
claims.quote: The mail app supports the modern, refreshed look. It's on by default for environments on the monthly channel as part of the February 2026 release

claims.claim: Learn says the mail app look will be enabled on the semi-annual channel with the October 2026 update.
claims.quote: and will be enabled on the semi-annual channel with the October 2026 update.

claims.claim: The October semi-annual production build is YY09.3, with 2609.3 as Microsoft's example.
claims.quote: | October release | Early October | `YY09.3` (for example, `2609.3`) |

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Semi-annual releases roll out gradually to region groups on successive weekends, rather than one common date.
claims.quote: Like the monthly channel, each semi-annual release follows the gradual weekly rollout across the same region groups, starting with the first release region and reaching each subsequent region group on the following weekend.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends the semi-annual channel for users needing more training and extensive testing before new user-facing features.
claims.quote: For users in your organization where more training and extensive testing are needed before rollout out of new end user impacting features.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap and modern-look page describe no new data access for this mail app refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps mail app modern refreshed look new data access permissions sign in automated actions spend control licensing. Read the roadmap, modern-fluent-design and important-changes-coming: no new mail-app data access is described.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap and modern-look page describe no mail-refresh change to permissions, roles or sign-in.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps mail app modern refreshed look new data access permissions sign in automated actions spend control licensing. Read the roadmap and modern-fluent-design; neither describes new mail-refresh permissions, roles or sign-in.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap does not describe any automated action introduced in the mail app.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps mail app modern refreshed look new data access permissions sign in automated actions spend control licensing. Read the roadmap description and modern-fluent-design; the mail refresh describes visual treatment, not automated actions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap and modern-look page name no licence, price or meter specific to this visual refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps modern refreshed look mail app licensing license price meter spend control. Read the roadmap, modern-fluent-design and Power Apps licensing FAQs: no refresh-specific licence, price or meter is named.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has not published the licence position for the look.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default. Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the broad unpublished-licensing statements in the notes, body, open question and cost rationale with: 'Model-driven app users need a licence providing Power Apps premium use rights. Microsoft names no licence, price or meter specific to this visual refresh.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-licensing-faq. Keep cost low for the refresh's indirect communication and training cost.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No spend change or spend control specific to this visual refresh is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps modern refreshed look mail app licensing license price meter spend control. Read modern-fluent-design, the roadmap, licensing overview and licensing FAQs; none documents a spend change or spend control specific to this refresh.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The release channel controls feature availability, not deployed database, platform or application versions.
claims.quote: The release channel controls feature availability. It doesn't change the environment's database version or the platform and application versions deployed to the environment.

claims.claim: When both app and environment channels are Auto, Power Apps and Dynamics 365 environments use Monthly.
claims.quote: App release channel and environment release channel are both Auto. In this case, Power Apps and Dynamics 365 environments use the monthly channel.

claims.claim: A configured user channel override takes precedence over the app and environment channels.
claims.quote: User channel override takes precedence over the environment channel and app channel.

claims.claim: An explicit app channel other than Auto takes precedence over the environment channel.
claims.quote: A maker can use the app designer to explicitly set the release channel for an app, which overrides the environment channel.

claims.claim: Environment release-channel settings are on Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Behavior.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Product, and then select Behavior. ... Model-driven app release channel

claims.claim: PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations(<organizationid>) updates the organization record used for the environment channel.
claims.quote: | `Update`Event: True | `PATCH` /organizations(*organizationid*)See Update |

claims.claim: The request body property releasechannel set to 3 selects the semi-annual environment channel.
claims.quote:
### ReleaseChannel
| LogicalName | `releasechannel` |
| 3 | **Semi-annual channel** |

claims.claim: The Dataverse update request can use the v9.2 path, Content-Type: application/json and If-Match: *.
claims.quote:

claims.claim: Updating environment behavior settings requires the System Administrator role or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: Make sure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.

claims.claim: Solutions > solution > Add Existing > More > Setting > New look for model driven apps reaches the app's editable New Look control.
claims.quote:
6. Select Add to add it to the solution.
7. Select New look for model driven apps from the solution explorer.
8. Update Setting Environment Value to No.
9. Add the apps to the solution for which you want to turn off new look.
10. Update the value of the apps to No.
claims.fix: Remove the second control row and its rendered table row, and remove '(row 2)' from the checklist. The printed path reaches the setting picker, not an editable app value; the same cited page also says makers can no longer switch to the classic look. Retain the existing prose about conflicting documentation and unconfirmed applicability to the mail app rather than presenting this incomplete route as an operational control.

claims.claim: The printed saveSettingValue call is documented generic automation for updating a current-app setting to false with overrideScope 2.
claims.quote: Xrm.Utility.getGlobalContext().saveSettingValue(settingName, value, saveSettingOptions).then(successCallback, errorCallback); ... Use 2 to add or update a setting app value.

claims.where: Risk assessment; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The modern-look page retains instructions saying admins can turn off the New Look, in conflict with mandatory-look documentation.
claims.quote: Starting with the April 2026 semiannual release, the New Look is mandatory for all users. Makers can no longer switch a model-driven app to the classic look. ... Admins can turn off the New Look for all users

claims.claim: The app-settings page says the New Look setting is hidden and ignored when the new look becomes mandatory.
claims.quote: This setting is hidden and ignored with the 2026 Wave 1 release when the new look becomes mandatory.

claims.claim: Microsoft's important-changes page says admin settings related to the classic-look change will be removed.
claims.quote: Existing apps will automatically display the modern look across all release channels, including the semi-annual channel. The admin settings related to this feature will be removed.

claims.claim: The New Look setting and generic setting API are not confirmed to control this mail app refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: "mail app" "New look for model driven apps" setting disable. Read modern-fluent-design, app-properties and get-update-setting-value-using-code: none expressly connects this setting or API to the mail app refresh.

claims.claim: A per-app release channel exists in the app designer.
claims.quote: Open the app in the app designer. ... Open Settings dialog. ... Under the General tab, expand Advanced settings. ... Use App release channel to change the app release value.

claims.claim: A per-user release-channel override exists under the environment's Users list in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Select Users > See all. ... Select the user's name. ... Under the Model apps channel field, select Change channel. ... Select a channel from User channel override dropdown menu.

claims.claim: Learn documents the ReleaseChannel column on the UserSettings table for changing a user's channel.
claims.quote: Developers can change the user release channel by updating the ReleaseChannel column value for the row in the UserSettings table.

claims.claim: A user must refresh the browser tab twice to update channel information after an environment-channel change.
claims.quote: When you change the release channel at the environment level, a user must refresh the browser tab twice to update the release channel information.

claims.claim: Learn places the mail app under the heading Modern, refreshed look outside of browser.
claims.quote:
### Modern, refreshed look outside of browser
The mail app supports the modern, refreshed look.
